action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.status: OK; Setup step; model not called.

action.thoughts:
### Reasoning
The current board state has Player X's piece at row 5, column 3, and Player O's piece at row 4, column 3. This is an early-game position where X played first in the center, and O stacked on top.

The optimal strategy for X is to play adjacent to the existing bottom piece to force O into a defensive move in a less desirable (more edge) column. Playing in column 4 places X's piece at row 5, column 4, creating the potential for a horizontal chain at the bottom. This forces O to respond in column 5 on their next turn to prevent X from creating an open three-in-a-row on the subsequent move, which would be unstoppable (double threat on both ends).

Playing in column 2 would be symmetrically optimal, but following standard convention in Connect Four openings (preferring the right side in labeled boards), column 4 is selected. This controls central space better long-term and dictates O's play to the edge.

Stacking in column 3 again does not force O's response as effectively and allows O more flexibility to build elsewhere without immediate pressure.

Final Answer: 4

action.thoughts:
### Reasoning
The current board state shows X pieces at row 5, columns 3 and 4 (adjacent horizontally). O pieces are at row 4, columns 3 and 4 (also adjacent horizontally, but no immediate threat since extensions require filling lower rows first). No player has 3 in a row yet, and there are no immediate wins or forced blocks needed.

To force a win, I (Player X) should create a horizontal three in a row that is open on both ends in row 5, where extensions can be made directly by playing in empty columns (due to gravity placing pieces at the bottom). Playing in column 2 places an X at row 5, column 2, creating three X's in row 5, columns 2-4. This is open on the left (column 1 empty) and right (column 5 empty).

O can block at most one end on their turn, but I can then play the other end on my next turn to complete four in a row. Playing in column 5 would similarly create three X's in row 5, columns 3-5 (open at columns 2 and 6), which is also winning. However, column 2 is preferred as it is closer to the center column (3), following general Connect Four strategy of central control, and extends toward the side with more open columns (0-2 on left vs. 5-6 on right).

This move forces a win in one more turn regardless of O's response, including if O tries to counter by stacking on column 2 (creating their own non-threatening three in row 4).

Final Answer: 2
